summary: Customer reports unexpected billing delta after API key tag rename affecting usage attribution
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a ~27% negative billing delta on their Feb 28 provisional invoice after renaming API key tags across multiple service accounts. The charges were attributed to a legacy org ID instead of their primary org, causing a provisional overcharge and missing reserve/burst credits on the final invoice.

Impact: LexaHealth is seeing an unexpected invoice variance (~$4,300) and missing application of scheduled reserved-burst credits for several 3-hour windows during Feb 25-27. This affects reconciliation for month-end close and blocks autopay. Customer is on an enterprise contract and requires an itemized explanation and corrective credit.

Environment: Production (us-east). Affected model traffic: mixture of hosted chat (redwood/gptx-8k) and batch embeddings (open/embedding-128). Activity timeframe: 2026-02-25 03:00 - 2026-02-27 12:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer renamed API key tags via Console API on 2026-02-24 at ~22:10 UTC (bulk tag rename from "production-team" to "lexa-prod").
2) We observed postback delivery succeeding but a subset of postbacks contained the old tag metadata in the payload (postback.source.tag = "production-team").
3) Billing attribution pipeline mapped tag to org/ledger and routed usage to legacy org ID 10124 instead of customer org 90211 for the outlier postbacks.
4) Invoice generation aggregated those lines under legacy org, leading to missing credits and an apparent overage on the customer's provisional invoice.

Expected behavior: Tag rename should atomically update the metadata mapping used by the postback pipeline; postbacks after rename should be attributed to customer org 90211 with reserved/burst credits applied.

Actual behavior: 8.3k postbacks (~2.6M tokens) were misattributed. Some postbacks were tagged correctly; others retained the old tag because of a race in the key metadata cache during the rename rollout.

Logs/attachments: Customer provided provisional invoice and screenshots; attached server-side postback logs and sample hashed request_ids.

Customer request: Detailed explanation of what caused the misattribution, an itemized reconciliation, and immediate provisional credit while engineering completes root-cause and rebackfill.

2026-03-11: Cache TTL was set incorrectly after last deploy (default 30m, but some edge frontends had 45m due to metrics race).
2026-03-11: Reprocessing design: idempotent re-eval of postbacks using authoritative mapping table; re-attribution should restore credits and stitch lines into LexaHealth ledger.

resolution: Provisional credit issued for $4,300 on 2026-03-12 while backfill completes. Root cause: race between console tag rename and api-key-metadata cache invalidation, combined with an elevated cache TTL on some frontends. Permanent fix: deploy cache-invalidation hook in Console rename path and set consistent TTL; add a monitoring alert for tag-mapping mismatch rates. Follow-up ticket created for the engineering rollout: INT-4410. Final reconciliation lines to be posted in this ticket when backfill job finishes.
